Baseball.why: k shrinks the difference between two clubs' season log-odds; 0.50 reflects that a best-of-series meeting between a .636 and a .605 club is close. Home edge 0.16 in logit units is the long-run MLB home-field figure (~54%).

Ice Hockey.why: Points-percentage log-odds shrunk by 0.55 (an 11-game sample is noisy) plus a 0.20 home term (~55% home win rate in the NHL).

Snooker.why: Strength is a 0-100 blend of frames won in this event (50%) and a rank score (37-position)/36 where the player is inside the published top 36 (50%). The 2.40 coefficient maps a 0.20 strength gap onto roughly a 61% best-of-7 win chance.

Rugby Union.why: No league table was readable, so the strength term is switched off entirely and only a 0.12 home term is applied. Confidence is capped at Low.

field.why: Outright weight = (points + 10)^1.5. The offset keeps zero-point drivers priced as longshots rather than at infinite odds; the exponent prices a 340-point leader at roughly 22% in a 23-driver field.

band.note: Brief: focus on selections priced between -250 (1.40) and +10000 (101.0).

items.text: The Islanders are 5-3-1 and have banked 11 of a possible 18 points, while Los Angeles arrive at UBS Arena with one win in seven (1-4-2) and only four points from 14. Our originated moneyline makes New York a 72.1% shot at 1.39, so the selection is the Islanders to win the match outright, not the puck line.

Minnesota carry a 6-2-2 record and 14 points from 20 into the Scotiabank Saddledome, where Calgary sit 2-6-0 with four points from 16. That is the widest points-percentage gap on tonight's board, so the model makes the Wild 70.5% to win and we back Minnesota on the moneyline at 1.42.

items.start_published: Thu 22 Oct, 08:00 (WST clock, no zone published)
items.text: Kyren Wilson is the world No. 9 on GBP 716,800 and has conceded only two frames in reaching Round 3, beating Ben Mertens 4-0 and Thepchaiya Un-Nooh 4-2. Pang Junxu, ranked 29, needed a deciding frame to see off Liam Davies. Wilson to win the match at 1.41 is our pick.

items.start_published: Thu 22 Oct, 14:00 (WST clock, no zone published)
items.text: Mark Williams, world No. 8 with GBP 747,400 on the published ranking list, has won both his matches by the same 4-2 scoreline, against Robbie Williams and Zhang Anda. Martin O'Donnell is outside the top 36 but has already removed Judd Trump and Luca Brecel this week. We still make Williams a 73.7% favourite at 1.36.

The safest route into the Scotiabank Saddledome game is Minnesota on the puck line. Their 6-2-2 start is worth 14 points against Calgary's four, and the goal-difference distribution puts the Wild within one goal or better in 82.6% of simulations. That makes plus 1.5 goals a 1.21 shot.

Florida are 5-2-2 and have collected 12 of 18 points; Pittsburgh are 3-6-1 with seven from 20 and sit bottom of their division on the fetched record. Giving the Panthers a 1.5-goal start at PPG Paints Arena is the pick, modelled at 79.7% and priced at 1.26.

Vancouver's 2-8-1 start is the worst record on the twelve-game slate, five points from a possible 22. Detroit are only 3-3-3 but have avoided regulation defeats more often than the Canucks, so giving the Red Wings a 1.5-goal cushion at 1.26 - a 79.2% model chance - is the play at Rogers Arena.

Vegas have opened 8-3-0 for 16 points from 22 and now visit a St. Louis side sitting on nine points from 18. Our margin model gives the Golden Knights a 77.9% chance of avoiding a defeat by two or more, which is why the 1.5-goal start is priced at 1.28 for the Enterprise Center game.

The Rangers are 7-3-1 for 15 points from 22, Toronto 5-4-2 for 12 from 22, and the model actually prefers New York on the road. Taking the Rangers on a 1.5-goal handicap at 1.32 covers a one-goal defeat in Toronto, which our goal-difference distribution puts at 75.6%.

Utah are 7-3-0 with 14 points from 20 and Seattle 6-3-1 with 13 from 20, so the two clubs are separated by a single point at Climate Pledge Arena. In a game this tight the plus 1.5 goal start matters: the Mammoth cover in 73.4% of our simulations, priced at 1.36.

Winnipeg arrive at 4-3-2 with ten points and Dallas at 5-3-1 with 11, a gap small enough that the model refuses to separate them by a full goal. Taking the Jets with a 1.5-goal start, a 70.6% cover chance at 1.42, is the selection at American Airlines Center.

items.start_published: Thu 22 Oct, 09:00 (WST clock, no zone published)
items.text: Slessor is the world No. 23 on GBP 329,200 and has dropped a single frame in two matches, 4-0 against He Guoqiang then 4-1 against Joe O'Connor. Ricky Walden, outside the published top 36, has beaten Neil Robertson 4-1 and Joe O'Connor 4-3. Slessor to win at 1.48 is the call.

Boston are 7-2-1 for 15 points from 20 and Nashville 3-2-3 for eight from 16, and the Bruins have home ice at TD Garden. The model puts Boston at 69.1% on the moneyline, which is the highest win probability of any home side on the slate after the Islanders.

items.start_published: Thu 22 Oct, 15:00 (WST clock, no zone published)
items.text: Jak Jones is ranked 24 with GBP 319,300 and has lost two frames in the event, 4-1 over Tom Ford and 4-2 over John Higgins. Daniel Wells, outside the top 36, has beaten Barry Hawkins 4-2 and Ryan Day 4-3. Back Jones in the match-winner market at 1.52, a 65.8% model chance.

Edmonton are 7-1-1 and have 15 points from 18, the best points percentage on the board alongside Carolina's 17 from 22. The Oilers have home ice at Rogers Place, and the model gives them 60.1% against a Hurricanes side that has played two more games. Edmonton to win at 1.66.

New Jersey are 5-4-0 while Anaheim are 4-5-0, and the Devils have home ice at the Prudential Center. The model separates them by six percentage points and prices New Jersey at 1.64 on the moneyline, a 61.0% chance, which is a Medium-confidence pick rather than a High one.

Milwaukee finished the regular season 103-59 (.636) and Tampa Bay 98-64 (.605), and the Brewers have home field at American Family Field for this World Series game. The gap is real but small, so the model makes Milwaukee only 55.6% at 1.80; the run line is the better angle than the moneyline.

items.start_published: Sun 25 Oct, race 16:00 track time (F1 publishes session times in track-local time only)
items.text: Antonelli leads the drivers' championship on 340 points after seventeen rounds, 102 clear of Mercedes team-mate George Russell on 238, with Hamilton on 229 and Verstappen on 221. Round 18 is the United States Grand Prix at the Circuit of The Americas over 56 laps. He is our race-winner selection at 4.51, but 22.2% is a Low-confidence price.
